Dir 1.1.text: Any implementation-defined behaviour on which the output of the program depends shall be documented and understood

Dir 2.1.text: All source files shall compile without any compilation errors

Dir 3.1.text: All code shall be traceable to documented requirements

Dir 4.2.text: All usage of assembly language should be documented

Dir 4.3.text: Assembly language shall be encapsulated and isolated

Dir 4.4.text: Sections of code should not be commented out

Dir 4.5.text: Identifiers in the same name space with overlapping visibility should be typographically unambiguous

Dir 4.6.text: typedefs that indicate size and signedness should be used in place of the basic numerical types

Dir 4.7.text: If a function returns error information, then that error information shall be tested

Dir 4.8.text: If a pointer to a structure or union is never dereferenced within a translation unit, then the implementation of the object should be hidden

Dir 4.9.text: A function should be used in preference to a function-like macro when they are interchangeable

Rule 1.1.text: The program shall contain no violations of the standard C syntax and constraints, and shall not exceed the implementation's translation limits

Rule 1.2.text: Language extensions should not be used

Rule 1.3.text: There shall be no occurrence of undefined or critical unspecified behaviour

Rule 2.1.text: A project shall not contain unreachable code

Rule 2.2.text: There shall be no dead code

Rule 2.3.text: A project should not contain unused type declarations

Rule 2.4.text: A project should not contain unused tag declarations

Rule 2.5.text: A project should not contain unused macro declarations

Rule 2.6.text: A function shall not contain unused label declarations

Rule 2.7.text: There should be no unused parameters in functions

Rule 3.1.text: The character sequences /* and // shall not be used within a comment

Rule 3.2.text: Line-splicing shall not be used in // comments

Rule 4.1.text: Octal and hexadecimal escape sequences shall be terminated

Rule 5.2.text: Identifiers declared in the same scope and name space shall be distinct

Rule 5.3.text: An identifier declared in an inner scope shall not hide an identifier declared in an outer scope

Rule 5.5.text: Identifiers shall be distinct from macro names

Rule 5.6.text: A typedef name shall be a unique identifier

Rule 5.7.text: A tag name shall be a unique identifier

Rule 5.8.text: Identifiers that define objects or functions with external linkage shall be unique

Rule 5.9.text: Identifiers that define objects or functions with internal linkage should be unique

Rule 6.1.text: Bit-fields shall only be declared with an appropriate type

Rule 6.2.text: Single-bit named bit fields shall not be of a signed type

Rule 7.1.text: Octal constants shall not be used

Rule 7.2.text: A u or U suffix shall be applied to all integer constants that are represented in an unsigned type

Rule 7.3.text: The lowercase character l shall not be used in a literal suffix

Rule 7.4.text: A string literal shall not be assigned to an object unless the objects type is pointer to const-qualified char

Rule 8.2.text: Function types shall be in prototype form with named parameters

Rule 8.3.text: All declarations of an object or function shall use the same names and type qualifiers

Rule 8.4.text: A compatible declaration shall be visible when an object or function with external linkage is defined

Rule 8.5.text: An external object or function shall be declared once in one and only one file

Rule 8.6.text: An identifier with external linkage shall have exactly one external definition

Rule 8.7.text: Functions and objects should not be defined with external linkage if they are referenced in only one translation unit

Rule 8.8.text: The static storage class specifier shall be used in all declarations of objects and functions that have internal linkage

Rule 8.9.text: An object should be defined at block scope if its identifier only appears in a single function

Rule 8.10.text: An inline function shall be declared with the static storage class

Rule 8.11.text: When an array with external linkage is declared, its size should be explicitly specified

Rule 8.12.text: Within an enumerator list, the value of an implicitly-specified enumeration constant shall be unique

Rule 8.13.text: A pointer should point to a const-qualified type whenever possible

Rule 8.14.text: The restrict type qualifier shall not be used

Rule 9.1.text: The value of an object with automatic storage duration shall not be read before it has been set

Rule 9.2.text: The initializer for an aggregate or union shall be enclosed in braces

Rule 9.3.text: Arrays shall not be partially initialized

Rule 9.4.text: An element of an object shall not be initialized more than once

Rule 9.5.text: Where designated initializers are used to initialize an array object the size of the array shall be specified explicitly

Rule 10.1.text: Operands shall not be of an inappropriate essential type

Rule 10.2.text: Expressions of essentially character type shall not be used inappropriately in addition and subtraction operations

Rule 10.3.text: The value of an expression shall not be assigned to an object with a narrower essential type or a different essential type category

Rule 10.4.text: Both operands of an operator in which the usual arithmetic conversions are performed shall have the same essential type category

Rule 10.5.text: The value of an expression should not be cast to an inappropriate essential type

Rule 10.6.text: The value of a composite expression shall not be assigned to an object with wider essential type

Rule 10.7.text: If a composite expression is used as one operand of an operator in which the usual arithmetic conversions are performed then the other operand shall not have wider essential type

Rule 10.8.text: The value of a composite expression shall not be cast to a different essential type category or a wider essential type

Rule 11.1.text: Conversions shall not be performed between a pointer to a function and any other type

Rule 11.2.text: Conversions shall not be performed between a pointer to an incomplete type and any other type

Rule 11.3.text: A cast shall not be performed between a pointer to object type and a pointer to a different object type

Rule 11.4.text: A conversion should not be performed between a pointer to object and an integer type

Rule 11.5.text: A conversion should not be performed from pointer to void into pointer to object

Rule 11.6.text: A cast shall not be performed between pointer to void and an arithmetic type

Rule 11.7.text: A cast shall not be performed between pointer to object and a non-integer arithmetic type

Rule 11.8.text: A cast shall not remove any const or volatile qualification from the type pointed to by a pointer

Rule 11.9.text: The macro NULL shall be the only permitted form of integer null pointer constant

Rule 12.1.text: The precedence of operators within expressions should be made explicit

Rule 12.2.text: The right hand operand of a shift operator shall lie in the range zero to one less than the width in bits of the essential type of the left hand operand

Rule 12.3.text: The comma operator should not be used

Rule 12.4.text: Evaluation of constant expressions should not lead to unsigned integer wrap-around

Rule 13.1.text: Initializer lists shall not contain persistent side effects

Rule 13.2.text: The value of an expression and its persistent side effects shall be the same under all permitted evaluation orders

Rule 13.3.text: A full expression containing an increment (++) or decrement (--) operator should have no other potential side effects other than that caused by the increment or decrement operator

Rule 13.4.text: The result of an assignment operator should not be used

Rule 13.5.text: The right hand operand of a logical && or || operator shall not contain persistent side effects

Rule 13.6.text: The operand of the sizeof operator shall not contain any expression which has potential side effects

Rule 14.1.text: A loop counter shall not have essentially floating type

Rule 14.2.text: A for loop shall be well-formed

Rule 14.3.text: Controlling expressions shall not be invariant

Rule 14.4.text: The controlling expression of an if statement and the controlling expression of an iteration-statement shall have essentially Boolean type

Rule 15.1.text: The goto statement should not be used

Rule 15.2.text: The goto statement shall jump to a label declared later in the same function

Rule 15.3.text: Any label referenced by a goto statement shall be declared in the same block, or in any block enclosing the goto statement

Rule 15.4.text: There should be no more than one break or goto statement used to terminate any iteration statement

Rule 15.5.text: A function should have a single point of exit at the end

Rule 15.6.text: The body of an iteration-statement or a selection-statement shall be a compound-statement

Rule 15.7.text: All if  else if constructs shall be terminated with an else statement

Rule 16.1.text: All switch statements shall be well-formed

Rule 16.2.text: A switch label shall only be used when the most closely-enclosing compound statement is the body of a switch statement

Rule 16.3.text: An unconditional break statement shall terminate every switch-clause

Rule 16.4.text: Every switch statement shall have a default label

Rule 16.5.text: A default label shall appear as either the first or the last switch label of a switch statement

Rule 16.6.text: Every switch statement shall have at least two switch-clauses

Rule 16.7.text: A switch-expression shall not have essentially Boolean type

Rule 17.1.text: The features of <stdarg.h> shall not be used

Rule 17.2.text: Functions shall not call themselves, either directly or indirectly

Rule 17.3.text: A function shall not be declared implicitly

Rule 17.4.text: All exit paths from a function with non-void return type shall have an explicit return statement with an expression

Rule 17.5.text: The function argument corresponding to a parameter declared to have an array type shall have an appropriate number of elements

Rule 17.6.text: The declaration of an array parameter shall not contain the static keyword between the [ ]

Rule 17.7.text: The value returned by a function having non-void return type shall be used

Rule 17.8.text: A function parameter should not be modified

Rule 18.1.text: A pointer resulting from arithmetic on a pointer operand shall address an element of the same array as that pointer operand

Rule 18.2.text: Subtraction between pointers shall only be applied to pointers that address elements of the same array

Rule 18.3.text: The relational operators >, >=, < and <= shall not be applied to objects of pointer type except where they point into the same object

Rule 18.4.text: The +, -, += and -= operators should not be applied to an expression of pointer type

Rule 18.5.text: Declarations should contain no more than two levels of pointer nesting

Rule 18.6.text: The address of an object with automatic storage shall not be copied to another object that persists after the first object has ceased to exist

Rule 18.7.text: Flexible array members shall not be declared

Rule 18.8.text: Variable-length array types shall not be used

Rule 19.1.text: An object shall not be assigned or copied to an overlapping object

Rule 19.2.text: The union keyword should not be used

Rule 20.1.text: #include directives should only be preceded by preprocessor directives or comments

Rule 20.2.text: The ',  or \ characters and the /* or // character sequences shall not occur in a header file name

Rule 20.3.text: The #include directive shall be followed by either a <filename> or \filename\ sequence

Rule 20.4.text: A macro shall not be defined with the same name as a keyword

Rule 20.6.text: Tokens that look like a preprocessing directive shall not occur within a macro argument

Rule 20.7.text: Expressions resulting from the expansion of macro parameters shall be enclosed in parentheses

Rule 20.8.text: The controlling expression of a #if or #elif preprocessing directive shall evaluate to 0 or 1

Rule 20.9.text: All identifiers used in the controlling expression of #if or #elif preprocessing directives shall be #define'd before evaluation

Rule 20.10.text: The # and ## preprocessor operators should not be used

Rule 20.11.text: A macro parameter immediately following a # operator should not immediately be followed by a ## operator

Rule 20.12.text: A macro parameter used as an operand to the # or ## operators, which is itself subject to further macro replacement, shall only be used as an operand to these operators

Rule 20.13.text: A line whose first token is # shall be a valid preprocessing directive

Rule 20.14.text: All #else, #elif and #endif preprocessor directives shall reside in the same file as the #if, #ifdef or #ifndef directive to which they are related

Rule 21.1.text: #define and #undef shall not be used on a reserved identifier or reserved macro name

Rule 21.2.text: A reserved identifier or macro name shall not be declared

Rule 21.3.text: The memory allocation and deallocation functions of <stdlib.h> shall not be used

Rule 21.4.text: The standard header file <setjmp.h> shall not be used

Rule 21.5.text: The standard header file <signal.h> shall not be used

Rule 21.6.text: The Standard Library input/output functions shall not be used

Rule 21.7.text: The atof, atoi, atol and atoll functions of <stdlib.h> shall not be used

Rule 21.8.text: The library functions abort, exit, getenv and system of <stdlib.h> shall not be used

Rule 21.9.text: The library functions bsearch and qsort of <stdlib.h> shall not be used

Rule 21.10.text: The Standard Library time and date functions shall not be used

Rule 21.11.text: The standard header file <tgmath.h> shall not be used

Rule 21.12.text: The exception handling features of <fenv.h> should not be used

Rule 22.1.text: All resources obtained dynamically by means of Standard Library functions shall be explicitly released

Rule 22.2.text: A block of memory shall only be freed if it was allocated by means of a Standard Library function

Rule 22.3.text: The same file shall not be open for read and write access at the same time on different streams

Rule 22.4.text: There shall be no attempt to write to a stream which has been opened as read-only

Rule 22.5.text: A pointer to a FILE object shall not be dereferenced

Rule 22.6.text: The value of a pointer to a FILE shall not be used after the associated stream has been closed

Rule 22.7.text: The macro EOF shall only be compared with the unmodified return value from any Standard Library function capable of returning EOF

Rule 22.8.text: The value of errno shall be set to zero prior to a call to an errno-setting-function

Rule 22.9.text: The value of errno shall be tested against zero after calling an errno-setting-function

Rule 22.10.text: The value of errno shall only be tested when the last function to be called was an errno-setting-function
